reports.title: The Ceasefire That Keeps Shooting
reports.subtitle: US and Iran are exchanging fire in the Strait of Hormuz while both sides insist a ceasefire is still in effect. One of them is lying, or neither knows what a ceasefire means.

reports.title: The Second Time a Court Killed Trump's Tariffs
reports.subtitle: The Court of International Trade struck down Trump's replacement 10% global tariffs. He appealed within 24 hours. The question is no longer whether courts will stop him, but whether it matters.

reports.title: Thailand's National AI Strategy Was a Chip Laundering Operation
reports.subtitle: US prosecutors believe OBON Corp, the centerpiece of Thailand's AI national strategy, moved $2.5 billion in Nvidia-equipped servers to China for Alibaba. The export controls were not beaten by spies; they were beaten by a trade show partner.

reports.title: The FCC vs. The View, and the Broadcast License as a Weapon
reports.subtitle: The Trump FCC is using a 1934 equal-time rule to investigate a talk show, threatening licenses and rewriting 20-year-old precedents. ABC is fighting back. The stakes are whether the government can police broadcast content through regulatory intimidation.

reports.title: France Opens Criminal Case Against Musk and X. He Still Isn't Coming.
reports.subtitle: French prosecutors escalated their probe of Elon Musk and X to a criminal investigation after he and former CEO Linda Yaccarino ignored summons. The US government previously called the probe a political attack on an American business.

reports.title: The White House Wants an FDA for AI. The Problem Is That Anthropic Wrote the Prescription.
reports.subtitle: A single model from Anthropic alarmed the VP, scrambled the administration's deregulatory posture, and may hand the biggest AI companies a regulatory moat they've been building toward for years.

reports.title: One Year After Operation Sindoor, Pakistan's Army Chief Is Having Lunch at the White House
reports.subtitle: India launched precision strikes on Pakistan a year ago and claims strategic victory. But the country it was trying to isolate is now being embraced by the same mediator who stopped the war.

reports.title: China's Exports Hit a Monthly Record While Trump Is Flying to Beijing to Demand Concessions
reports.subtitle: China's April export surge was driven partly by buyers front-loading against Iran war supply disruptions. It also gives Xi Jinping a stronger hand at next week's summit than any tariff threat could have produced.

reports.title: The GUARD Act Passed Committee 22-0. It Would Also Require All Adults to Show ID Before Using a Chatbot.
reports.subtitle: Framed as child protection, the bill advancing through the US Senate would build a national ID database for AI access. The same architecture is being replicated in Australia, Ireland, and the UK simultaneously.

reports.title: Trump's Three-Day Ceasefire Is a Victory Photo, Not a Peace Deal
reports.subtitle: Russia and Ukraine just agreed to stop shooting for 72 hours so Putin can celebrate Victory Day in peace. Polymarket says a durable ceasefire is 25% likely by year-end. Both sides know why.

reports.title: Europe Just Gutted Its Own AI Law. Industry Called It 'Not Enough.'
reports.subtitle: The EU delayed its flagship AI regulations by 18 months, exempted industrial AI entirely, and banned nudification apps. Tech lobbyists and US officials wanted more. Centrist lawmakers agreed.

reports.title: Samsung Workers Want 15% of the AI Boom. Management Says the Company Can't Afford It.
reports.subtitle: Samsung's union is threatening an 18-day strike starting May 21, demanding a share of the HBM windfall that helped drive Korea's GDP. The company says paying out would hurt competitiveness. One of them is right.

reports.title: The EPA Deregulated 180 Polluters Via Email. It Called This the Biggest Deregulatory Action in US History.
reports.subtitle: ProPublica revealed that the Trump EPA granted two-year Clean Air Act exemptions to over 180 major industrial facilities through a simple email request system. The agency's own air quality scientists were sidelined.

reports.title: New York's Commuter Rail Is Seven Days From Its First Strike in 30 Years
reports.subtitle: Long Island Rail Road unions and the MTA agree on three years of raises but are deadlocked on year four. If talks fail by May 16, 300,000 daily riders lose their train.
